questions.question: Which description fits the **ImplementationGuide** resource?
options: A set of rules of how a particular interoperability or standards problem is solved - typically through the use of FHIR resources.
A search parameter that defines a named search item that can be used to search/filter on a resource.
A formal computable definition of an operation (on the RESTful interface) or a named query (using the search interaction).

This resource documents a set of capabilities (behaviors) of a FHIR Server for a particular version of FHIR that may be used as a statement of actual server functionality or a statement of required or desired server…
questions.explanation: **ImplementationGuide**: A set of rules of how a particular interoperability or standards problem is solved - typically through the use of FHIR resources. This resource is used to gather all the parts of an implementation guide into a logical whole and to publish a computable definition of all the parts. The other descriptions belong to **SearchParameter**, **OperationDefinition**, **CapabilityStatement**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? Package all the profiles, extensions and value sets for a national standard.
questions.explanation: **ImplementationGuide**. Gathers the parts of an IG into one computable definition.

questions.question: You know **ImplementationGuide**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “what a system must support”?
questions.explanation: **CapabilityStatement**: what a system must support. **ImplementationGuide** is for something else: A set of rules of how a particular interoperability or standards problem is solved - typically through the use of FHIR resources.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **ImplementationGuide** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of ImplementationGuide are `url` (1..1), `name` (1..1), `status` (1..1), `packageId` (1..1), `fhirVersion` (1..*). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **ImplementationGuide** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of ImplementationGuide: `status`. `status`: draft | active | retired | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
